items.title: Oscar Peterson interviewed by Joe Williams, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: the sound that they made from Otto Hardwicke to all of the guys.

ctx.x: But Lester Young was also another, he was an instigator. He loved pianists. I remember there was a young man on the tour by the name of Bobby, well he’s a pianist, we used to call him “Bobby Socks.” And I remember we were standing backstage playing one night and Bobby says, “hey Prez, do you know this tune?” and he started to play. And Prez came up behind him, he stood there and he looked, and he said, “Bobby Socks, I see what you’re doing with your right people, but what are you going to do with these left…

Oh yes he could play that thing. He used to love that thing. But Ben Webster, that was another case of — I think that we were so blessed to come through the time when we had those people to listen to, to appreciate, and just to make us lose ourselves in what they did. Because they were capable. Ellington — I’d get lost in his beauty, the beauty of the chords, the beauty of the way they and played together, the way they would breathe together, and the sound that they made from Otto Hardwicke to all of the guys.
